title: Restricting S3 Access Across an Organization
prompt: Grant read access to a bucket to the AWS account of the audit team. You want to avoid enumerating accounts in the policy if member accounts are replaced in the future. Within the organization, allow only the audit role. Which conditions should you use to grant access?

choices.text: Use only PrincipalOrgID as a condition
choices.explanation: This cannot narrow access to roles used for auditing within the organization.

choices.text: Set the organization's management account ID as the Principal
choices.explanation: This does not directly identify the audit role in a member account.

choices.text: Match aws:PrincipalOrgID and an audit-role pattern in aws:PrincipalArn using AND conditions
choices.explanation: You can validate organization membership and the accessing principal at the same time.

choices.text: Match aws:SourceOrgID and a role pattern
choices.explanation: SourceOrgID is for supported service-to-service calls and is not the condition for validating organization membership for direct role access.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: You can validate organization membership and the accessing principal at the same time.
learning.concept: PrincipalOrgID evaluates the principal's organization membership, and PrincipalArn evaluates the principal's ARN. For a request from a role session, PrincipalArn refers to the ARN of the original IAM role.

check.prompt: If a role with the same name is also created under another path in the organization, what should you narrow?
check.answer: Include the audit role's path in the PrincipalArn pattern.

title: Private Delivery Through CloudFront
prompt: You deliver paid videos through CloudFront. You want to grant each viewer access to multiple segments for only one hour and prevent direct access using S3 URLs. Which configuration is appropriate?

choices.text: Protect an S3 website endpoint with OAC
choices.explanation: OAC is configured with an S3 REST origin and cannot be applied to a website endpoint.

choices.text: Use CloudFront signed cookies to control the target paths and expiration
choices.explanation: They can protect many segment URLs under the same conditions.

choices.text: Make the entire S3 bucket publicly readable and validate signatures with CloudFront WAF
choices.explanation: Direct access to S3 does not pass through WAF.

choices.text: Block public access to S3 and use OAC and a bucket policy to allow the target distribution
choices.explanation: This prevents viewers from bypassing the origin directly.

choices.text: Enable Origin Shield
choices.explanation: This reduces origin load; it does not authenticate viewers.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: Signed cookies can protect many segment URLs under the same conditions. Viewers cannot bypass the origin directly.
learning.concept: Signed cookies authorize viewer access to CloudFront, while OAC signs requests from CloudFront to an S3 REST origin. On the S3 side, allow only the target distribution.

check.prompt: What if the download is a single file and the user cannot handle cookies?
check.answer: You can use a signed URL for the viewer. Continue using OAC for the origin.

title: Cross-account KMS read access
prompt: An account A S3 data set is encrypted with a customer managed KMS key. Only an ETL role in account B should be allowed to read it. S3 read access is already configured. Which additional permissions are required?

choices.text: Allow the ETL role in account B to decrypt in the key policy in account A.
choices.explanation: Trust from the key-owning account is required.

choices.text: Add kms:Decrypt to the S3 bucket policy.
choices.explanation: An S3 bucket policy cannot grant permission to use a KMS key.

choices.text: Switch account A's key to the AWS managed key aws/s3.
choices.explanation: You cannot edit the aws/s3 key policy to grant access to another account.

choices.text: Allow only kms:GenerateDataKey for the ETL role in account B.
choices.explanation: Reading existing objects requires decryption permission.

choices.text: Allow kms:Decrypt for account A's key in the IAM policy for the ETL role in account B.
choices.explanation: Cross-account access also requires the corresponding permission on the calling side.

source.label: AWS公式資料 · KMSのクロスアカウントアクセス

learning.reason: Trust from the key-owning account is required. Cross-account access also requires the corresponding permission on the calling side.
learning.concept: With SSE-KMS, S3 uses KMS to decrypt the data key. For cross-account access, check both the key-side trust and the caller-side IAM permission. Grant kms:Decrypt for reads.

check.prompt: You added GetObject to the bucket policy, but the decryption error remains. What should you check next?
check.answer: Identify the actual key used for encryption, then check its key policy and the calling role's IAM policy.

sourceLabel: Official AWS documentation · KMS cross-account access

title: ECS permission boundaries
prompt: A business container on ECS Fargate reads an SQS queue for orders. It must not receive permission to access a queue used by another job in the same service. ECS handles image retrieval from ECR and log delivery. Where should you assign the permissions?

choices.text: Grant all SQS and ECR permissions to the execution role.
choices.explanation: The container's SDK does not normally use the execution role credentials.

choices.text: Grant read access to the target SQS queue to the task role, and ECR and logging permissions to the task execution role.
choices.explanation: This lets you restrict API operations by the application and by the ECS infrastructure separately.

choices.text: Add SQS permissions to the shared EC2 instance profile for the cluster.
choices.explanation: With Fargate, you do not manage the execution infrastructure through a user instance profile.

choices.text: Allow all principals in the same VPC in the SQS policy.
choices.explanation: A network boundary alone cannot identify business jobs.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: This lets you restrict API operations by the application and by the ECS infrastructure separately.
learning.concept: The application SDK obtains credentials from the task role. The execution role is used for Fargate image retrieval and operations by the awslogs driver.

check.prompt: The application now needs to write to S3. Which role should receive the additional permission?
check.answer: Add the required write permission for the target bucket to the task role in the relevant task definition.

title: CloudFront caching and personal data
prompt: Static assets and a user-specific orders API are served under the same CloudFront domain. The orders API validates a Bearer token, and responses must not be shared across users. Keep caching for static assets enabled.

choices.text: Use only the URL path in the cache key for all paths, and forward Authorization.
choices.explanation: Even if the token reaches the origin, a cache hit could return the same response to another user.

choices.text: Do not forward Authorization; set only the API's Cache-Control to private.
choices.explanation: The origin cannot validate the token.

choices.text: Set the same long minimum TTL for the dynamic API and static files.
choices.explanation: This could override instructions to prevent caching of user-specific responses.

choices.text: Use a separate behavior for the API, disable caching, and forward Authorization.
choices.explanation: This preserves caching for the default static path and forwards credentials to the API.

source.label: AWS公式資料 · Authorizationヘッダーの転送

learning.reason: This preserves caching for the default static path and forwards credentials to the API.
learning.concept: A cache policy controls storage and the cache key. An origin request policy controls what else is forwarded. Path-based behaviors can separate static assets from the API.

check.prompt: You configured CachingDisabled, but authentication errors persist. What should you check?
check.answer: Check the policy that forwards Authorization to the origin. Disabling caching alone does not forward the authentication header.

sourceLabel: Official AWS documentation · Forwarding the Authorization header

title: Pod-specific permissions in EKS
prompt: An OIDC provider is already configured in an existing EKS cluster. Only the payment Pod needs to retrieve a specific Secrets Manager secret. You do not want to share the IAM role on the nodes with other Pods. Which configuration should you use if you cannot install an additional agent?

choices.text: Configure IRSA for the target ServiceAccount, and restrict the trust policy to the namespace and ServiceAccount.
choices.explanation: This uses the existing OIDC federation and scopes credentials to the Pod's principal.

choices.text: Grant secret retrieval permissions to the worker node IAM role.
choices.explanation: This does not isolate permissions for workloads on the same node.

choices.text: Switch to EKS Pod Identity without adding an agent.
choices.explanation: The Pod Identity Agent is required on typical EC2 worker nodes.

choices.text: Grant the ServiceAccount permission to get secrets with Kubernetes RBAC.
choices.explanation: This is permission to access the Kubernetes API; it does not authorize Secrets Manager operations.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: This uses the existing OIDC federation and scopes credentials to the Pod's principal.
learning.concept: IRSA integrates with the cluster's OIDC issuer. Restrict the IAM role's trust policy to the aud and ServiceAccount sub, and scope the permissions policy to the secret.

check.prompt: If the role's permissions policy is limited to the target secret, is it acceptable for other Pods to be able to assume the role?
check.answer: No. Limiting the resources a role can access and limiting who can use those permissions are separate requirements.

title: Accessing S3 from a private subnet
prompt: A batch process on EC2 needs to access S3 in the same Region. Internet routing is prohibited, and access should be limited to specific buckets. Which combination should you choose without adding hourly charges to the path used by the batch process?

choices.text: Create an S3 interface endpoint using PrivateLink
choices.explanation: This provides a private connection, but the endpoint incurs an hourly charge.

choices.text: Restrict the NAT gateway's destinations to S3 public addresses
choices.explanation: This does not eliminate the internet path and increases NAT charges.

choices.text: Create an S3 gateway endpoint and associate it with the batch process's route table
choices.explanation: It provides access to S3 in the same VPC and Region without traversing the internet.

choices.text: Restrict the target buckets with an endpoint policy
choices.explanation: An endpoint policy can limit which S3 resources are reachable through the endpoint.

choices.text: Add the bucket ARN to an S3 security group
choices.explanation: Security groups do not evaluate IAM resource ARNs.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: A gateway endpoint provides access to S3 in the same VPC and Region without traversing the internet. An endpoint policy can limit which S3 resources are reachable through the endpoint.
learning.concept: The gateway endpoint route uses S3's managed prefix list. An endpoint policy adds a restriction; it does not replace permissions in IAM or a bucket policy.

check.prompt: What should you check if you get a 403 even though the target bucket is reachable through the endpoint?
check.answer: The endpoint policy alone does not grant access. Check the role's permissions, the bucket policy, and KMS permissions if encryption is used.

title: Operational access without a bastion host
prompt: An operations team needs to open a shell on a private EC2 instance. They must not open inbound ports, users must be controlled through IAM, and shell session logs must be retained in CloudWatch Logs.

choices.text: Connect over SSH through an EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint
choices.explanation: This requires allowing inbound SSH, and shell output to CloudWatch must also be configured separately.

choices.text: Use a standard Systems Manager Session Manager session and configure the required VPC endpoints and logging
choices.explanation: IAM can control who can start a session, and a standard session can record shell input and output.

choices.text: Allow only SSH tunneling through Session Manager
choices.explanation: Session Manager cannot record the contents of an encrypted SSH tunnel session.

choices.text: Connect over SSH or RDP using Client VPN
choices.explanation: Inbound access must be allowed on the target, and session recording requires separate configuration.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: IAM can control who can start a session, and a standard session can record shell input and output.
learning.concept: Logs from a standard shell session can be sent to CloudWatch Logs. Session Manager cannot record the contents of SSH or port-forwarding sessions. In a private network, check the endpoints required for SSM and log delivery.

check.prompt: If CloudTrail records StartSession, can you also see the commands that were entered?
check.answer: The session start operation is traceable, but you must separately configure standard shell session logging to see commands and output.

title: Preventing data exfiltration
prompt: In member accounts in an organization, you do not want ordinary administrators to disable S3 Block Public Access. An approved security operations role should be exempt. Which method also applies to new accounts?

choices.text: Add a deny policy to each administrator's IAM user
choices.explanation: This makes it difficult to prevent gaps for new roles or accounts.

choices.text: Use an AWS Config managed rule to record noncompliance
choices.explanation: This detects the change after the fact and does not block the API call that disables the setting.

choices.text: Use an Organizations SCP to explicitly deny the operation, with a condition that exempts the approved role
choices.explanation: This applies a permissions boundary to member accounts under the OU and prevents administrators from disabling the setting.

choices.text: Use an Organizations tag policy to control public access settings
choices.explanation: Tag policies do not control the S3 Block Public Access API.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: An SCP applies a permissions boundary to member accounts under the OU and can prevent administrators from disabling the setting.
learning.concept: An SCP limits the maximum permissions available in member accounts and also applies to the root user of those accounts. The exempt role still needs a separate IAM permission to perform the operation.

check.prompt: Can the role perform the operation as soon as it is excluded from the SCP's Deny?
check.answer: The exemption only removes the SCP denial. Also confirm that the role has the required permissions.

title: Private API Gateway
prompt: Several services in a VPC call an API Gateway REST API. You want to prevent calls from any endpoint other than the permitted VPC endpoints, even if credentials are stolen.

choices.text: Set the REST API endpoint type to private and use an execute-api interface endpoint
choices.explanation: This allows access to the API without using a public route.

choices.text: Use a Regional API and configure CloudFront OAC for its origin
choices.explanation: This does not restrict direct API calls to specific VPC endpoints.

choices.text: Use CORS to allow the VPC CIDR
choices.explanation: CORS controls browser origins and cannot enforce the use of an endpoint.

choices.text: Use the API resource policy to explicitly deny requests when aws:SourceVpce is not on the allowlist
choices.explanation: This can deny access from an unintended endpoint even when IAM allows the request.

choices.text: Use the VPC NAT gateway's Elastic IP as the authentication method
choices.explanation: A source IP does not bind calls made with stolen credentials over another path to a VPC endpoint.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: A private API avoids a public route. The resource policy can deny access from an unintended endpoint even when IAM allows the request.
learning.concept: An interface endpoint provides a network path. Matching aws:SourceVpce in the API resource policy can exclude another endpoint in the same VPC.

check.prompt: If the permitted and unpermitted endpoints are in the same VPC, can SourceVpc distinguish them?
check.answer: No. Both have the same VPC ID, so use SourceVpce.

title: Immutable audit logs
prompt: Prevent even operations administrators from deleting audit logs for seven years. Amazon S3 must enforce a retention period against overwrites and version-specific deletions by administrators in the organization.

choices.text: Use only S3 Versioning and standard lifecycle rules
choices.explanation: A principal with sufficient permissions can delete a specified version.

choices.text: Set a retention period in compliance mode for S3 Object Lock
choices.explanation: This strictly prevents deletion of protected versions and shortening of their retention period before the retention expires.

choices.text: Use governance mode and grant administrators BypassGovernanceRetention
choices.explanation: Administrators with the bypass permission can circumvent retention.

choices.text: Transition the objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive
choices.explanation: A storage tier does not lock deletion operations.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: This strictly prevents deletion of protected versions and shortening of their retention period before the retention expires.
learning.concept: S3 Object Lock in compliance mode prevents deletion of protected versions until their retention period expires. A normal delete can add a delete marker, but the protected version remains.

check.prompt: How can you check whether an older version is retained when it is not visible in a GET request?
check.answer: List the object versions and check the retention settings on the relevant version. Even if the latest version is a delete marker, an older version may remain.

title: Rotating Lambda secrets
prompt: A Lambda function connects to RDS PostgreSQL. Credentials must be changed periodically, and the function must use the new values without being redeployed. The database is in a private subnet.

choices.text: Store the password in an encrypted environment variable and rotate the KMS key periodically
choices.explanation: Rotating a KMS key does not change the database password.

choices.text: Store the password in SSM SecureString and set only a value expiration policy
choices.explanation: Expiration does not synchronize a password change with the database user.

choices.text: Rotate the RDS credentials with Secrets Manager, and have Lambda retrieve the secret at runtime
choices.explanation: Once the database targeted by rotation is reachable, the value can be updated without redeploying the application.

choices.text: Store the value in an SSE-KMS object in S3 and enable versioning
choices.explanation: Encryption at rest and versioning alone do not change database credentials.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: Once the database targeted by rotation is reachable, the value can be updated without redeploying the application.
learning.concept: Secrets Manager rotation must also set the new value in the database. The application retrieves AWSCURRENT and, if cached credentials are stale, retrieves the secret again before connecting.

check.prompt: Will rotating only the KMS key prevent access with the old database password?
check.answer: No. KMS key rotation and changing the database password are independent operations.

title: Separating CloudTrail permissions
prompt: Aggregate management events from all Regions and all member accounts into an S3 bucket in a log archive account. Automatically include new accounts and prevent member administrators from stopping the recording.

choices.text: Enable event history in each account and manually save CSV files during audits
choices.explanation: This does not provide continuous aggregation or automatically cover new accounts.

choices.text: Create a separate CloudTrail trail for each member account
choices.explanation: Member-side administrators can often change this design.

choices.text: Configure only an AWS Config organization aggregator
choices.explanation: This aggregates configuration and compliance information, not API event trails.

choices.text: Create a CloudTrail multi-Region organization trail and deliver logs to the log archive S3 bucket
choices.explanation: The organization trail records and aggregates events across the organization, and member administrators cannot change it.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: The organization trail records and aggregates events across the organization, and member administrators cannot change it.
learning.concept: An organization trail and a multi-Region setting address separate concerns. To deliver logs to an S3 bucket in another account, allow delivery by that trail in the bucket policy.

check.prompt: Can an organization trail that records only management events also record S3 GetObject?
check.answer: GetObject is a data event. Configure data events for the relevant buckets according to the audit requirements.

title: Protecting an HTTP application behind an ALB
prompt: An HTTP application runs behind a public ALB. Control excessive request rates per IP address and SQL injection before requests reach the application. Exceptions must also be configurable by URL.

choices.text: Associate AWS WAF with the ALB and configure rate-based rules and SQLi inspection rules
choices.explanation: It can evaluate HTTP request contents and aggregation criteria, and scope rules to selected paths.

choices.text: Limit the request rate with the ALB security group
choices.explanation: A security group does not inspect request rates or HTTP payloads.

choices.text: Enable only AWS Shield Advanced and have it evaluate SQL syntax
choices.explanation: WAF rules perform application-layer SQLi inspection.

choices.text: Aggregate GuardDuty findings in Security Hub
choices.explanation: Security findings can be collected, but this does not block individual requests before they reach the application.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: It can evaluate HTTP request contents and aggregation criteria, and scope rules to selected paths.
learning.concept: A WAF rate-based rule aggregates requests by the specified key. Use scope-down statements to limit the paths included in the aggregation. Limit SQLi inspection to those same paths as well.

check.prompt: If the WAF aggregation key is shared across all IP addresses, can you limit only one user's high request rate?
check.answer: No. Aggregate by IP address to apply a per-IP limit.

title: Cross-account S3 uploads
prompt: A partner’s AWS role must deliver files to a receiving S3 bucket. The receiving account must automatically own the delivered objects, and the partner must be allowed to do nothing beyond uploading. Which configuration is not affected by ACL differences?

choices.text: Keep the Object Writer setting and grant read access through the bucket ACL
choices.explanation: The writer normally owns the objects, and the configuration still depends on ACLs.

choices.text: Use Bucket owner preferred and make the ACL header optional
choices.explanation: This cannot guarantee ownership of objects that do not include bucket-owner-full-control.

choices.text: Choose Bucket owner enforced and allow the partner role to use PutObject only for a specific prefix
choices.explanation: ACLs are disabled, the bucket-owning account owns the objects, and permissions can be limited to the required operation.

choices.text: Give the partner a read/write access point for the receiving S3 bucket
choices.explanation: This allows reading as well, although the requirement is delivery only.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: Disabling ACLs lets the bucket-owning account own the objects, while permissions can be limited to the required operation.
learning.concept: With Bucket owner enforced, ACLs are disabled and the bucket-owning account owns the objects. The PutObject Allow can be restricted to a specific prefix in the bucket.

check.prompt: Is PutObject alone enough to let the same partner list objects?
check.answer: Listing requires a separate s3:ListBucket permission. Do not grant it to this delivery-only role.

title: Restricting key use outside the organization
prompt: A business role can generate data keys. After limiting its permissions to the target KMS key, you want to prevent the role from calling KMS directly and allow use only through S3.

choices.text: Allow the VPC private CIDR with aws:SourceIp
choices.explanation: This does not determine whether the KMS call came through S3.

choices.text: Set the S3 service name for the target Region in kms:ViaService
choices.explanation: This can limit requests to those made through a supported service.

choices.text: Set kms:KeyOrigin to AWS_KMS
choices.explanation: This constrains the origin of the key material, not the call path.

choices.text: Set aws:PrincipalServiceName to S3 only
choices.explanation: Use ViaService to identify KMS operations performed by a service on the caller’s behalf.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: This can limit requests to those made through a supported service.
learning.concept: kms:ViaService is a condition for when a supported service uses KMS on a principal’s behalf. An Allow with an S3-specific condition does not apply to other services or direct requests to KMS.

check.prompt: You added an Allow conditioned on ViaService, but another policy also allows direct calls to KMS. What should you review?
check.answer: Evaluate both policies and remove the unconditional permission for direct access. A conditional Allow does not override another Allow.

title: User authentication and STS
prompt: Mobile users sign in with an existing OIDC IdP. You want to provide signed-in users with short-lived AWS credentials to access their own storage areas in S3. Keep the existing IdP.

choices.text: Use a Cognito user pool ID token as-is to sign S3 requests with Signature Version 4
choices.explanation: An ID token alone does not provide the signing keys for AWS API requests.

choices.text: Distribute CloudFront signed URLs to all users and allow any S3 operation
choices.explanation: A signed URL is not temporary credentials for arbitrary AWS API requests.

choices.text: Create an IAM user for each user and distribute long-term keys to the mobile app
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement for temporary credentials.

choices.text: Associate the OIDC IdP with a Cognito identity pool and configure an IAM role with an S3 prefix restriction for each identity
choices.explanation: This uses the existing user authentication and provides temporary AWS credentials with restricted permissions.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: This uses the existing user authentication and provides temporary AWS credentials with restricted permissions.
learning.concept: A Cognito identity pool uses federation to return temporary AWS credentials. Use an IAM role to restrict each user to their own S3 prefix. User pools primarily handle authentication tokens for applications.

check.prompt: Can you use a user pool ID token alone with the standard S3 SDK?
check.answer: No. You must obtain temporary AWS credentials separately to sign requests from the S3 SDK.

title: Reaching S3 from on premises
prompt: An on-premises audit server connects to S3 through a Site-to-Site VPN and a VPC. It must not route to S3 public IP addresses, and you want the lowest operational overhead while connecting to a private IP address.

choices.text: Place an S3 interface endpoint in the VPC and resolve its private DNS name from on premises over the VPN
choices.explanation: An interface endpoint is reachable over the VPN and does not require a public internet route to S3.

choices.text: Advertise the VPC’s S3 gateway endpoint over the VPN
choices.explanation: An on-premises host cannot use a gateway endpoint across a VPN.

choices.text: Route from on premises through the VPC NAT gateway to the public S3 endpoint
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to avoid public IP addresses.

choices.text: Disable Block Public Access on the S3 bucket and call its public URL over the VPN
choices.explanation: Changing the access setting does not provide a connection that avoids public IP addresses.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: An interface endpoint is reachable over the VPN and does not require a public internet route to S3.
learning.concept: An interface endpoint provides an ENI with a private IP address in a VPC subnet. Check the route from the VPN, DNS resolution, and the endpoint’s security group.

check.prompt: Name resolution works, but HTTPS over the VPN times out. What should you check?
check.answer: Check the path from on premises to the endpoint ENI and inbound permission for TCP port 443 on the endpoint.

title: Providing a service across VPCs
prompt: A shared service must be provided to multiple AWS accounts. The consumer VPCs have overlapping CIDR ranges with the provider VPC, and consumers must not be able to route to the provider's other subnets. Expose only the TCP application port.

choices.text: Create VPC Peering and advertise the entire CIDR range on both sides
choices.explanation: The connection cannot be established with overlapping CIDR ranges, and it shares connectivity at the network level.

choices.text: Connect both sides to a Transit Gateway and propagate the overlapping CIDR ranges to each other
choices.explanation: This design is unsuitable when routes overlap and does not expose a service by itself.

choices.text: Expose a provider-side NLB as a PrivateLink endpoint service, and create an interface endpoint on the consumer side
choices.explanation: This limits access to a specific TCP service and works even when CIDR ranges overlap.

choices.text: Move the service to an internet-facing ALB
choices.explanation: This does not provide access only to the provider's TCP service without routing over the public internet.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: The endpoint can be limited to a specific TCP service and works even when CIDR ranges overlap.
learning.concept: PrivateLink lets consumers access a service behind the provider's NLB through an interface endpoint in the consumer VPC, without creating routes to all of each other's subnets.

check.prompt: Can a consumer use this connection to SSH directly to another EC2 instance in the provider VPC?
check.answer: No. It provides an entry point to the exposed service; it does not route to arbitrary subnets.

title: Duplicate and out-of-order S3 events
prompt: Events for updates to the same S3 key are used to update a search index. Events can arrive out of order or more than once. What should you do to prevent an older event from overwriting the result of the latest update?

choices.text: Round event creation timestamps down to the minute and process events from the same minute in arrival order
choices.explanation: This cannot handle separate updates in the same minute or out-of-order delivery.

choices.text: Normalize and compare the S3 sequencer for the same key, and conditionally accept only updates newer than the stored value
choices.explanation: This lets you compare the order of object creation and deletion events for the same key, while conditional updates prevent concurrent processing conflicts.

choices.text: Send events from EventBridge to a standard SQS queue and assume they will be received in FIFO order
choices.explanation: A standard SQS queue does not guarantee ordering, and it does not correct events that were already out of order upstream.

choices.text: Compare S3 VersionId values as strings and choose the one that appears newest
choices.explanation: VersionId does not guarantee chronological ordering when compared lexicographically.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: You can compare the order of object creation and deletion events for the same key, and conditional updates prevent concurrent processing conflicts.
learning.concept: The sequencer in an S3 notification can be compared only for the same object key. If the values have different lengths, pad the shorter value on the left with zeros before comparing them.

check.prompt: Can you compare two events for different keys by the size of their sequencer values?
check.answer: No. A separate mechanism is needed to determine ordering across keys.

title: Duplicate payment processing
prompt: Orders are processed from SQS and retried on timeout. The payment API accepts the order ID as an idempotency key. How can you prevent multiple charges for one order while still allowing retries after a failure?

choices.text: Only increase the SQS visibility timeout
choices.explanation: This cannot prevent redelivery after a processing failure or a failure after payment succeeds but before the message is deleted.

choices.text: Delete the message from SQS before making the payment
choices.explanation: An order whose payment did not complete would not be retried.

choices.text: Pass the same idempotency key on every attempt for the same order, and delete the message only after the payment result is confirmed
choices.explanation: Retries are treated as the same payment, while an incomplete order can be processed again after redelivery.

choices.text: Rely only on SQS FIFO deduplication and generate a new payment ID for every attempt
choices.explanation: Producer-side deduplication does not eliminate retries in the consumer's processing.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: The payment API treats retries as the same payment, while an incomplete order can be processed again after redelivery.
learning.concept: FIFO send-side deduplication does not guarantee that an external API side effect occurs only once. Delete the message only after the payment result is confirmed.

check.prompt: What happens if a new idempotency key is generated for each timeout?
check.answer: The API treats each attempt for the same order as a separate operation, so duplicate charges are not prevented.

title: Availability and disaster recovery
prompt: An EC2 and RDS system must meet an RPO of a few minutes and an RTO of 30 minutes during a Regional outage. Keep the application capacity running in the standby Region to a minimum, while allowing health checks during normal operations.

choices.text: Replicate daily snapshots and create all services after an outage
choices.explanation: This is unlikely to meet an RPO of a few minutes and does not allow application health checks in advance.

choices.text: Use a Multi-AZ configuration in a single Region
choices.explanation: This handles an Availability Zone outage, but not an outage affecting the entire Region.

choices.text: Run both Regions continuously at full production capacity from the start
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to operate with minimal standby capacity.

choices.text: Continuously replicate the database across Regions, run a scaled-down application in the standby Region, and automate failover and scaling up
choices.explanation: A warm standby can support operational checks during normal conditions and enable rapid recovery.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: A warm standby supports operational checks during normal conditions and enables rapid recovery.
learning.concept: A warm standby runs a scaled-down environment that is promoted and scaled up during an outage. RPO is the time window of data loss; RTO is the time allowed for recovery.

check.prompt: If replication lag is 8 minutes, can you say that an RPO of 5 minutes has been met?
check.answer: No. Measure replication lag separately from the time needed for promotion and failover.

title: Ordering Within Groups and Parallel Processing
prompt: A request intake API must process change instructions in the correct order for each contract ID. Ordering across different contracts is unnecessary, and a slow operation for one contract should not prevent work on other contracts.

choices.text: Use an SQS FIFO queue with the contract ID as the MessageGroupId, processing messages sequentially within each group.
choices.explanation: This preserves order within each group while allowing different groups to be processed in parallel.

choices.text: Use the same MessageGroupId for every contract.
choices.explanation: This removes the ability to process different contracts in parallel.

choices.text: Put the contract ID on a standard SQS queue and apply updates in the order messages are received.
choices.explanation: A standard queue does not guarantee delivery order for a given contract.

choices.text: Use the event ID as the MessageGroupId and the contract ID as the DeduplicationId.
choices.explanation: This does not preserve order within a contract, and distinct changes could be treated as duplicates.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: This preserves order within each group while allowing different groups to be processed in parallel.
learning.concept: In FIFO queues, MessageGroupId defines the ordering group. DeduplicationId is used to deduplicate sends; it does not determine instruction order.

check.prompt: What happens if every contract uses the same MessageGroupId?
check.answer: Ordering is enforced across a broader scope, but a slow contract can block processing for other contracts and reduce parallelism.

sourceLabel: AWS Official Exam Guide (Exam Content Outline)

title: Partial Failures in SQS Batches
prompt: A Lambda function processes a standard SQS queue. If only 1 of 10 messages fails, you need to avoid both reprocessing the 9 successful messages and losing the failed message.

choices.text: Catch function exceptions and always return an empty response.
choices.explanation: All messages are treated as successful, so the failed message may also be deleted.

choices.text: Enable ReportBatchItemFailures in the event source mapping and return the ID of the failed message.
choices.explanation: This reports the partial failure, allowing successful messages to be deleted and only the failed message to be retried.

choices.text: Shorten the visibility timeout and fail the entire batch with an exception.
choices.explanation: The entire batch is retried, not just the failed message.

choices.text: Delete all 10 messages before processing them.
choices.explanation: The failed message can no longer be retried from the queue.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: This reports the partial failure, allowing successful messages to be deleted and only the failed message to be retried.
learning.concept: Use partial batch responses for an SQS event source mapping. Standard SQS queues provide at-least-once delivery, so idempotency is still required when handling partial failures.

check.prompt: What happens to successful records in the batch if the function throws an exception that reaches the caller?
check.answer: The entire batch is treated as failed. Handle exceptions for individual records and return a list of the failed IDs.

sourceLabel: AWS Official Exam Guide (Exam Content Outline)

title: Internet Egress During an AZ Failure
prompt: Web workers in private subnets across three AZs maintain outbound connections to external APIs. You want to avoid an AZ failure stopping traffic from other AZs and avoid cross-AZ data transfer charges. Use zonal NAT gateways.

choices.text: Provision one zonal NAT gateway and share it across all three AZs.
choices.explanation: This creates a dependency on that AZ and NAT gateway, and traffic from other AZs incurs cross-AZ data transfer.

choices.text: Place a NAT gateway in each AZ, but point all subnet routes to a single NAT gateway.
choices.explanation: Even with NAT gateways in the other AZs, normal routing concentrates traffic in one AZ.

choices.text: Configure an S3 gateway endpoint for the external APIs.
choices.explanation: It does not provide routes to arbitrary external internet APIs.

choices.text: Place a zonal NAT gateway in each AZ and route each private subnet to the NAT gateway in the same AZ.
choices.explanation: This avoids dependence on a single AZ and avoids cross-AZ paths to the NAT gateways.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: This avoids dependence on a single AZ and avoids cross-AZ paths to the NAT gateways.
learning.concept: With a zonal design, route tables for subnets in each AZ send traffic to a NAT gateway in that same AZ. Each NAT gateway's EIP is the source IP visible to external services.

check.prompt: What if all subnets point to the same NAT gateway, even though three are provisioned?
check.answer: Egress is effectively concentrated in one AZ. Check each private subnet's route, not just the gateway placement.

sourceLabel: AWS Official Exam Guide (Exam Content Outline)

title: Safe ECS Deployments
prompt: An ECS HTTP service must maintain existing connections and avoid routing traffic to new tasks until they are ready to process requests. If a bad deployment is detected, it should automatically return to the last successful version. Use ECS rolling updates.

choices.text: Adjust the ALB health checks and deregistration delay.
choices.explanation: Traffic can be sent to ready targets, while in-flight requests on old tasks are given time to complete.

choices.text: Set the minimum healthy percentage to 0%.
choices.explanation: All old tasks could be stopped first, making it difficult to maintain connections.

choices.text: Enable rollback for the ECS deployment circuit breaker.
choices.explanation: It can detect a deployment that fails to reach a steady state and roll back to the last successful deployment.

choices.text: Use only critical findings from ECR image scanning to determine whether to deploy.
choices.explanation: Static image findings do not determine whether the application starts or passes health checks.

choices.text: Only increase the Route 53 TTL.
choices.explanation: This does not affect target readiness or deployment outcomes for targets behind the same ALB.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: Traffic can be sent to ready targets, while in-flight requests on old tasks are given time to complete. A deployment that fails to reach a steady state can be detected and rolled back to the last successful version.
learning.concept: ALB health checks and deregistration delay govern traffic handling. The ECS deployment circuit breaker handles deployment failure detection and rollback to a completed version.

check.prompt: Is a health check that returns HTTP 200 immediately after the process starts sufficient?
check.answer: Not if the application is not yet ready to handle business requests. The health check needs to reflect readiness.

sourceLabel: AWS Official Exam Guide (Exam Content Outline)

title: Exclude an Unhealthy Endpoint with DNS
prompt: Use Region A as the primary and Region B as the standby. Do not send user traffic to B under normal conditions, and fail over to B if the ALB in A becomes unhealthy.

choices.text: Publish A and B using latency-based routing
choices.explanation: B could be selected even under normal conditions.

choices.text: Use Route 53 failover routing and configure target health evaluation for the ALB
choices.explanation: Route 53 can return the primary under normal conditions and a healthy secondary when the primary is unhealthy.

choices.text: Use geolocation routing to assign the entire world to A
choices.explanation: This does not by itself define a standby failover when an outage occurs.

choices.text: Set an extremely long DNS record TTL and add A and B to the same record
choices.explanation: This is unsuitable for keeping traffic on the primary normally and switching quickly during an outage.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: Route 53 can return the primary under normal conditions and a healthy secondary when the primary is unhealthy.
learning.concept: Route 53 failover routing changes the DNS response destination. DNS responses already cached by clients and existing connections do not change immediately.

check.prompt: Why might some users still connect to the old ALB after failover?
check.answer: DNS caches or existing connections may persist. Distinguish new DNS responses from the connections clients actually make.

title: Redis Failover
prompt: A surge in cache misses can bring down the database, so avoid a design that switches to an empty cache when the primary fails. Use cross-AZ automatic promotion with ElastiCache for Valkey.

choices.text: Use a primary-only configuration and take daily snapshots
choices.explanation: This does not provide synchronous standby promotion during an AZ outage, and the cache will become stale.

choices.text: Place a client cache in the application in the same AZ
choices.explanation: It shares the same AZ failure and does not provide a standby cache server.

choices.text: Enable Multi-AZ and automatic failover in a replication group with a replica in a different AZ
choices.explanation: Promoting the replica can preserve the existing cache to the extent possible.

choices.text: Copy backups to another Region and restore manually each time
choices.explanation: This does not provide automatic promotion within the same Region or a quick failover.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: Promoting the replica can preserve the existing cache to the extent possible.
learning.concept: ElastiCache automatic failover promotes a replica. With asynchronous replication, there is no guarantee that every cache update made immediately before a failure will be retained.

check.prompt: Would adding a replica in the same AZ absorb an outage affecting the entire AZ?
check.answer: No. To account for an AZ outage, place the replica in a different AZ.

title: Redundant On-Premises Connectivity
prompt: The primary connection is AWS Direct Connect, and on-premises networks connect to VPCs behind a Transit Gateway. You cannot provision a second dedicated connection, but you need to reach the same network even if the dedicated connection fails.

choices.text: Create a second VIF on the same Direct Connect physical connection
choices.explanation: This does not provide redundancy against failure of the same physical connection.

choices.text: Make the VPN depend only on the same physical path as Direct Connect
choices.explanation: It would be affected by the same failure as the primary connection.

choices.text: Add a second NAT gateway
choices.explanation: This does not provide a redundant route from the on-premises network.

choices.text: Connect a Site-to-Site VPN to the TGW over an independent internet connection and configure dynamic routing
choices.explanation: This provides a separate path and allows traffic to switch to the VPN when the primary route is withdrawn.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: This provides a separate path and allows traffic to switch to the VPN when the primary route is withdrawn.
learning.concept: Use an independent connection for the Site-to-Site VPN, and control normal-operation preference and failover after route withdrawal with dynamic routing such as BGP.

check.prompt: Would adding a VIF on the same Direct Connect provide protection against a disconnection?
check.answer: It may add a route at the configuration level, but it does not provide redundancy against a physical connection failure.

title: Writes During a Regional Outage
prompt: Applications in two Regions read and write user profiles during normal operation. If the Region receiving writes becomes unavailable, you want writes to continue by changing the connection to the other Region. You accept a last-writer-wins outcome if conflicts occur. AWS should manage bidirectional replication and conflict resolution.

choices.text: Configure a DynamoDB global table with multi-Region eventual consistency
choices.explanation: Each replica can accept writes, and conflicts are resolved using last-writer-wins.

choices.text: Enable DynamoDB point-in-time recovery (PITR) and send all requests to a single Region
choices.explanation: This does not provide concurrent writes in another Region or immediate failover.

choices.text: Treat ordinary Aurora read replicas as independent writers in both Regions
choices.explanation: Read replicas cannot be treated as independent writers at the same time.

choices.text: Copy only cross-Region changes from DynamoDB Streams to independent tables
choices.explanation: This requires custom handling to prevent replication loops and resolve conflicts. Global tables meet these requirements as a managed service.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: Each replica can accept writes, and conflicts are resolved using last-writer-wins.
learning.concept: With DynamoDB global tables using MREC, each Region accepts writes, replicates them asynchronously, and resolves conflicts. This does not combine concurrent updates in the application.

check.prompt: Immediately after a write in another Region, will every Region always return the same value?
check.answer: MREC does not guarantee that. Check whether the design can tolerate replication lag.

title: Retrying a Multi-Step Workflow
prompt: An order is processed in this sequence: authorize payment, reserve inventory, and confirm shipment. If shipment confirmation fails, the inventory must be released, and transient errors should be retried with exponential backoff. The execution history must also show which step failed.

choices.text: Create a separate EventBridge rule for each operation and track completion order only through monitoring
choices.explanation: Failure paths and the order of compensating actions cannot be managed centrally.

choices.text: Use Step Functions Standard with Retry and Catch, branching to a compensation task on failure
choices.explanation: It retains execution state and history and lets you define retries and compensation for each step.

choices.text: Implement all operations in Lambda and always rerun the entire function from the beginning
choices.explanation: It is difficult to manage step-level retries or compensate for steps that have already completed.

choices.text: Only send failure notifications with CloudWatch alarms
choices.explanation: This does not retry steps or release inventory.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: It retains execution state and history and lets you define retries and compensation for each step.
learning.concept: Standard supports long-running executions and execution history. Retry handles retries, while Catch transitions to error handling; an explicitly defined compensation task releases the inventory.

check.prompt: If shipment fails after inventory has been reserved, will Step Functions release the inventory automatically?
check.answer: No. Implement inventory release in the transition target of Catch.

title: Replaying Kinesis Data
prompt: Multiple consumers process events while maintaining their own processing history. After deploying new aggregation logic, you want to reprocess the original events going back 7 days. Keep the checkpoints for normal processing intact.

choices.text: Use standard SQS to make messages visible again after they have been deleted
choices.explanation: Deleted messages cannot be retrieved.

choices.text: Keep Kinesis retention at 24 hours and set the starting position to TRIM_HORIZON
choices.explanation: This cannot retrieve data beyond the retention period.

choices.text: Set Kinesis Data Streams retention to at least 7 days and have a separate consumer reread the data from the relevant time
choices.explanation: Retained data can be replayed independently of the progress of existing consumers.

choices.text: Change only the filter in EventBridge Pipes
choices.explanation: This does not create records for the 7 days of data that have already been lost.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: Retained data can be replayed independently of the progress of existing consumers.
learning.concept: Consumers can reread records retained in Kinesis Data Streams. Data that has already expired cannot be recovered by extending the retention period afterward.

check.prompt: If you extend 24-hour retention to 7 days today, can you read data from last week?
check.answer: No. Data that has already expired cannot be read. Set the required retention period in advance.

title: S3 Protection and Recovery
prompt: You need to recover older versions deleted by operational error and access the data from another Region if a Region is lost. Existing objects must also be included, and erroneous delete markers must not be applied to the destination.

choices.text: Enable S3 Versioning on the source and destination, and configure CRR with delete marker replication disabled
choices.explanation: This replicates new objects without applying the specified delete markers at the destination.

choices.text: Transition objects to S3 One Zone-IA
choices.explanation: This is a single-AZ storage class and does not create a replica in another Region.

choices.text: Copy objects to another prefix in the same bucket in the Region
choices.explanation: This does not protect against a Regional outage.

choices.text: Configure live CRR only; existing objects will be replicated automatically
choices.explanation: Existing objects from before the configuration require a separate process, such as Batch Replication.

choices.text: Use S3 Batch Replication to replicate existing objects
choices.explanation: This can backfill existing data that was not included in live replication.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: This replicates new objects without applying the specified delete markers at the destination. Live replication targets that did not include existing data can be backfilled.
learning.concept: CRR uses versioning on both buckets. Use Batch Replication to backfill existing objects, and control delete marker replication through the replication configuration.

check.prompt: If one new sample object is replicated, can you conclude that migration of existing objects is complete?
check.answer: No. Check the batch results and the inventory of objects in scope separately.

title: RDS Restore Point
prompt: A mistaken update occurred at noon on an RDS PostgreSQL database in the same Region. You want to restore the data from immediately before the failure to a separate instance for verification, then compare it while keeping the production database running.

choices.text: Roll back the Multi-AZ standby to a point before noon
choices.explanation: The synchronous standby also reflects mistaken updates, so it cannot be used for a restore to an arbitrary point in time.

choices.text: Overwrite the production database in place with a snapshot from just before the update
choices.explanation: The requirement is to keep the production database running, and restoration does not overwrite it in place.

choices.text: Only promote a read replica
choices.explanation: Promotion does not restore to a specified point in time, and the update may already have reached the replica.

choices.text: Perform a point-in-time restore from an RDS automated backup to create a new database
choices.explanation: Transaction logs are used to create a separate database at the specified point in time while keeping the production database intact.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: Transaction logs are used to create a separate database at the specified point in time while keeping the production database intact.
learning.concept: RDS PITR creates a new database at a specified point within the retention window. Standbys and replicas normally reflect updates, so they are not equivalent to restoring to a chosen point in time.

check.prompt: If the mistaken update has also reached the replica, can promoting it undo the update?
check.answer: No. Use PITR to restore to a specified point before the mistaken update.

title: EventBridge Delivery Failures
prompt: Audit events are delivered from EventBridge to a processing destination. If an IAM permission issue lasts beyond the retry period, you need to preserve the failed events so you can investigate the cause and process them again.

choices.text: Only set the target's retry count to the maximum
choices.explanation: There is no place to preserve events after retries are exhausted.

choices.text: Configure an SQS standard queue as the target's DLQ and allow EventBridge to send messages through the queue policy
choices.explanation: The DLQ can retain events that could not be delivered and their error information.

choices.text: Configure only a notification for failures after an asynchronous invocation of Lambda succeeds
choices.explanation: This does not capture failures that occur while EventBridge is trying to deliver to the target.

choices.text: Retain only CloudWatch metrics
choices.explanation: You can see the number of failures, but you cannot reprocess the event payloads.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: A DLQ can retain events that could not be delivered and their error information.
learning.concept: An EventBridge target DLQ retains undelivered events and error information. Lambda's asynchronous failure destination handles failures after Lambda has accepted an invocation.

check.prompt: EventBridge cannot invoke Lambda because of insufficient permissions. What happens if only Lambda has a failure destination?
check.answer: The invocation failed before Lambda accepted it, so it does not go there. Configure a DLQ on the EventBridge target.

title: Static Content Delivery During a Regional Failover
prompt: The same static site has been replicated in advance to two Regions behind CloudFront. If the primary S3 REST origin returns a specified 5xx status code, you want CloudFront to send GET requests to the standby origin without changing users' URLs.

choices.text: Create a CloudFront origin group and configure 5xx status codes as failover criteria
choices.explanation: The same distribution can fail over to a secondary origin when a specified method fails.

choices.text: Add the S3 URL to the cache key using a CloudFront origin request policy
choices.explanation: Forwarding settings for headers or query strings do not implement failover when an error occurs.

choices.text: Allow access from both Regions in the S3 bucket policy
choices.explanation: Permissions do not select which origin CloudFront connects to.

choices.text: Send S3 events to SNS
choices.explanation: Object event notifications do not provide HTTP failover for read requests.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: The same distribution can fail over to a secondary origin when a specified method fails.
learning.concept: Origin group failover takes effect when a configured error occurs. The supported methods are GET, HEAD, and OPTIONS; this mechanism is not for arbitrary write operations.

check.prompt: Will a POST write automatically fail over to another destination in the same group?
check.answer: No. Design a separate approach for failover of write operations.

title: RDS Connection Storm
prompt: Thousands of Lambda functions start within a short period, and RDS PostgreSQL reaches its maximum connection count. Keep the existing SQL unchanged, manage credentials, and reuse connections. There is spare capacity in storage and CPU.

choices.text: Add a read replica and send all writes to it
choices.explanation: Writes go to the writer, and a read replica does not reuse connections.

choices.text: Increase EBS IOPS
choices.explanation: This does not directly address the concurrent connection limit.

choices.text: Add RDS Proxy between Lambda and RDS
choices.explanation: It pools database connections and decouples high Lambda concurrency from the number of database connections.

choices.text: Use only API Gateway caching
choices.explanation: This cannot prevent connection spikes for calls that are not cached, such as update operations.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: It pools database connections and decouples high Lambda concurrency from the number of database connections.
learning.concept: RDS Proxy pools connections to the underlying database and can reuse them across clients when conditions permit. Session state that causes pinning and long transactions can reduce reuse efficiency.

check.prompt: Will database connections always stay at a fixed count if you add a proxy?
check.answer: No. Pinning or the number of concurrent transactions may require many database connections.

title: DynamoDB Write Skew
prompt: Order events are written to DynamoDB. A large, steady volume of writes for a particular tenant is concentrated on a single partition key, causing throttling even though the table has spare capacity overall. A change that queries multiple shards for reads is acceptable.

choices.text: Add a distribution suffix to the tenant ID to spread writes across partition keys
choices.explanation: This design removes the concentration of writes on a single hot key.

choices.text: Only increase the table's capacity
choices.explanation: Spare capacity across the table does not by itself resolve the throughput limit of a single physical partition.

choices.text: Add DAX to speed up write processing
choices.explanation: DAX is primarily a low-latency read cache and does not spread persistent writes for a hot key.

choices.text: Use the same tenant ID as the partition key again in a GSI
choices.explanation: This leaves the concentration on the base table and may also create skew in the index.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: This design removes the concentration of writes on a single hot key.
learning.concept: Adding a distribution value to a key through write sharding can reduce skew. To read all items for a tenant, you must issue a Query to every shard and combine the results.

check.prompt: What is a drawback of increasing the number of shards?
check.answer: Retrieving all items requires querying more destinations. Choose the number of shards by balancing write distribution against read cost.

title: Sustained EBS IOPS
prompt: A database with 800 GiB of data is stored on a single volume. It requires sustained 32,000 IOPS rather than burst performance, along with consistently low latency. The instance meets the bandwidth requirements of each option. Which configuration should be used when 99.999% volume durability is also required?

choices.text: Use gp2 at 800 GiB
choices.explanation: The baseline performance at this size is below the requirement.

choices.text: Provision io2 Block Express for at least 32,000 IOPS
choices.explanation: It is suited to workloads that need high provisioned IOPS and low latency.

choices.text: Use st1 and rely on short bursts
choices.explanation: It is a sequential-throughput HDD volume and is not suited to sustained, high random IOPS.

choices.text: Use instance store as a persistent volume
choices.explanation: It does not provide persistence across instance stops or host failures.

source.label: AWS公式資料 · EBS SSDタイプの比較

learning.reason: This use case calls for high provisioned IOPS and low latency.
learning.concept: io2 Block Express provides high sustained IOPS and 99.999% designed durability. Check the EC2 instance's EBS bandwidth and IOPS limits as well as the volume settings.

check.prompt: If measured performance does not improve after setting the required IOPS, what should you check?
check.answer: Check the instance's EBS limits, throughput as determined by I/O size, queue depth, and other relevant factors.

sourceLabel: AWS official material · Comparison of EBS SSD types

title: Shared files for Linux
prompt: Linux EC2 instances in multiple Availability Zones scale in and out while concurrently updating a shared set of files. The existing application uses POSIX permissions and file locking. Capacity cannot be determined in advance.

choices.text: Have the application use S3 directly and acquire the existing POSIX locks
choices.explanation: S3 uses an object API and cannot preserve existing POSIX file locking.

choices.text: Attach the same EBS gp3 volume to EC2 instances in every Availability Zone
choices.explanation: EBS is an Availability Zone-scoped resource, and gp3 does not support Multi-Attach.

choices.text: Place local EBS volumes in each Availability Zone and run rsync overnight
choices.explanation: This does not provide concurrent updates or shared locking.

choices.text: Use EFS Regional and place a mount target in each Availability Zone
choices.explanation: Linux clients in multiple Availability Zones can use a shared NFS file system without preallocating capacity.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: Linux clients in multiple Availability Zones can use shared NFS storage whose capacity does not need to be preallocated.
learning.concept: EFS Regional provides a shared NFS file system and stores data and metadata across multiple Availability Zones. Mount targets are the access points for connecting from each Availability Zone.

check.prompt: If an EFS One Zone file system can be accessed from another Availability Zone, does that mean its data is stored in multiple Availability Zones?
check.answer: No. The Availability Zones from which it can be accessed are separate from the Availability Zone where the file data is stored.

title: S3 uploads from around the world
prompt: Users upload large videos from every continent to S3 in a single Region. Choose a design that improves transfer times over long-distance paths and avoids resending the entire file after a failure.

choices.text: Increase the GET cache TTL in CloudFront
choices.explanation: Download caching settings do not improve upload transfer or retries.

choices.text: Use S3 Intelligent-Tiering and pin objects to the FA tier
choices.explanation: This is a storage tier for after objects are stored, not a way to improve long-distance transfers.

choices.text: Use an S3 Transfer Acceleration endpoint
choices.explanation: It can route transfers through a nearby edge location and the AWS network.

choices.text: Configure S3 Cross-Region Replication to the destination
choices.explanation: This replicates objects after S3 receives them; it does not improve the initial upload path.

choices.text: Use S3 multipart upload and retry individual parts
choices.explanation: Only failed parts need to be retransmitted, and parts can be transferred in parallel.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: Transfer Acceleration can use a transfer path through a nearby edge location and the AWS network. Multipart upload lets clients retransmit only failed parts and can transfer parts in parallel.
learning.concept: Transfer Acceleration provides a path through edge locations. With multipart upload, manage the UploadId and the result for each part, retry only failed parts, and complete the upload at the end.

check.prompt: Can Transfer Acceleration alone resume a single PUT from where it stopped?
check.answer: No. It improves the transfer path; multipart upload is needed to reduce how much data must be retransmitted.

title: Aurora read scaling
prompt: Read traffic on an Aurora writer has increased, and order writes are slow. You want to offload reads from the application to multiple replicas, within the acceptable read-replica lag. The number of replicas should scale up or down automatically with load.

choices.text: Deploy an Aurora Global Database and change the write region
choices.explanation: Its primary purpose is not dynamic read distribution within the same Region.

choices.text: Use Aurora Auto Scaling to adjust the number of read replicas, and use the reader endpoint for read connections
choices.explanation: The reader endpoint selects connection targets, and the read capacity can be adjusted.

choices.text: Pin all clients to the reader instance endpoint
choices.explanation: New connections cannot be distributed to replicas added later.

choices.text: Pool SQL connections to the writer with RDS Proxy and send all SQL to that writer
choices.explanation: This reduces connection management overhead, but query execution load remains on the writer and the replica count does not scale automatically.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: The reader endpoint selects connection targets while the number of read replicas is adjusted to meet demand.
learning.concept: Aurora Auto Scaling adjusts the number of read replicas. The reader endpoint distributes new connections, so SQL statements are not distributed across replicas when a single long-lived connection is used.

check.prompt: Why might reporting queries concentrate on one replica even when there are four?
check.answer: The reporting connection pool may be reusing the same connection. Check connection lifetime and the number of connections.

title: Caching for a High-Read, Frequently Updated API
prompt: The product details API receives a high volume of reads for the same SKU. A brief delay after a price update is acceptable, and the database is queried on a cache miss. The design must not lose database updates if the cache is lost during a failure.

choices.text: Use cache-aside with ElastiCache, keeping the database as the durable source of truth and configuring a TTL or invalidation on updates
choices.explanation: Confirm updates in the database and serve repeated reads from the cache.

choices.text: Use the cache alone as the durable source of truth for prices, without writing to the database
choices.explanation: Price updates cannot be guaranteed to survive if the cache is lost.

choices.text: Use a local cache on each EC2 instance with no expiration
choices.explanation: Updates do not propagate to other nodes, so the brief-staleness requirement cannot be met.

choices.text: Re-export every SKU to S3 in a batch process on every read
choices.explanation: This adds substantial processing for repeated reads of the same SKU.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: Confirm updates in the database and serve repeated reads from the cache.
learning.concept: With cache-aside, a cache miss reads from the database and places the result in the cache. A short TTL or invalidation on update manages freshness; DB overload during a cache failure requires separate planning.

check.prompt: What is the risk of a design that keeps the latest value only in the cache and writes it to the database later?
check.answer: A failure before the write-back can lose an update that appeared to have been committed.

title: Isolated Reads in Kinesis
prompt: Five Kinesis consumers read the same shard. The existing real-time detection consumer must not be affected by heavy reads from another consumer. The producer-side shard assignment cannot be changed.

choices.text: Extend only the record retention period
choices.explanation: This does not eliminate the sharing of read throughput.

choices.text: Have the producer write the same event five times
choices.explanation: This increases write load, but consumers still share the read capacity for the same shard.

choices.text: Register the detection consumer for Enhanced Fan-Out
choices.explanation: A registered consumer gets dedicated read throughput per shard.

choices.text: Increase the checkpoint update interval for all consumers
choices.explanation: This does not isolate read bandwidth.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: A registered consumer gets dedicated read throughput per shard.
learning.concept: Registered Enhanced Fan-Out consumers use dedicated read throughput for each shard. Changing the retention period does not increase the read capacity.

check.prompt: Would extending the retention period for a backfill isolate the detection consumer's bandwidth?
check.answer: No. Retention controls how long data can be reread; Enhanced Fan-Out separates read capacity.

title: Lambda Initialization Latency
prompt: A production API uses an alias for a Java Lambda function. The peak period is known in advance, and a certain number of initialized execution environments must be available at the start of the peak.

choices.text: Configure Reserved Concurrency only
choices.explanation: This reserves or limits concurrency but does not guarantee initialized execution environments.

choices.text: Increase the function timeout
choices.explanation: This does not eliminate initialization latency for requests.

choices.text: Add more function URLs and remove per-alias allocations
choices.explanation: Adding endpoints does not initialize execution environments in advance.

choices.text: Schedule Provisioned Concurrency for the alias to start shortly before the peak
choices.explanation: The specified number of initialized environments can be prepared by the scheduled time.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: The specified number of initialized environments can be prepared by the scheduled time.
learning.concept: Reserved Concurrency reserves or limits concurrency. Provisioned Concurrency reserves initialized environments for a specific version or alias and incurs charges while it is provisioned, even when unused.

check.prompt: Does setting Reserved Concurrency to 200 eliminate cold starts?
check.answer: No. It reserves concurrency capacity but does not guarantee that the environments are initialized.

title: Scaling Capacity Ahead of Traffic
prompt: An EC2 Auto Scaling application has low load until just before noon every day, followed by a predictable surge exactly at noon. New instances take 8 minutes to begin processing requests. The goal is to minimize the initial queue buildup.

choices.text: Create a scheduled action to increase capacity sufficiently ahead of the set time
choices.explanation: Initialization can finish before traffic arrives.

choices.text: Use ordinary dynamic scaling after the CPU threshold is exceeded at noon
choices.explanation: Capacity increases only after the instance startup delay.

choices.text: Set only the instance warmup period to 8 minutes
choices.explanation: This adjusts how metrics are evaluated after new instances launch; it does not schedule them to launch in advance.

choices.text: Run health checks at intervals shorter than the instance startup time
choices.explanation: This does not increase available capacity in advance.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: Initialization can finish before traffic arrives.
learning.concept: A scheduled action changes capacity at a specified time. Warmup affects how metrics for new instances are handled; it does not start them earlier.

check.prompt: What if the start time is unknown but long-term cyclical demand has been observed?
check.answer: Predictive scaling can be considered if there is enough data. A time-based schedule is suitable for a known, isolated event.

title: Reducing read volume for analytics queries
prompt: Read only a subset of columns from the past day's JSON logs in Amazon S3 using Athena. You do not need to retrieve every field in each record. Choose the changes that will reduce the amount of data scanned and query execution time.

choices.text: Combine all logs into one gzip-compressed JSON file
choices.explanation: This is not suitable for selecting columns or skipping data by date.

choices.text: Convert the logs to Parquet
choices.explanation: A columnar format lets Athena scan primarily the columns that are needed.

choices.text: Omit the WHERE clause from every query
choices.explanation: This prevents data from being skipped based on the date.

choices.text: Partition the logs by date and filter on the date key in the query
choices.explanation: Only the partition for the relevant date needs to be scanned.

choices.text: Replicate the target S3 data using Versioning
choices.explanation: Versioning does not reduce the amount of data Athena reads.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: A columnar format lets Athena scan primarily the columns that are needed. Only the partition for the relevant date needs to be scanned.
learning.concept: In Athena, including a date partition in the query condition narrows the data scanned. Parquet's columnar format reduces reads of unnecessary columns.

check.prompt: Does simply gzip-compressing JSON let Athena physically read only the required columns?
check.answer: No. Compression reduces storage size, while a columnar format enables Athena to skip columns.

title: Global TCP ingress
prompt: A custom TCP application runs in two Regions. A business partner's firewall allows traffic only to a small number of fixed IPv4 addresses, and you do not want failover during a Regional outage to depend on DNS caching.

choices.text: Expose an NLB using only a low-TTL Route 53 record
choices.explanation: This depends on clients' DNS caches and does not provide a shared, fixed ingress IP.

choices.text: Use a CloudFront origin group
choices.explanation: CloudFront is not a transparent forwarding service for arbitrary custom TCP traffic.

choices.text: Configure the NLBs in both Regions as endpoints in Global Accelerator
choices.explanation: Global Accelerator accepts traffic on fixed Anycast IP addresses and can route TCP traffic to healthy endpoints.

choices.text: Hard-code a Region-specific EIP on each client
choices.explanation: There is no shared ingress point to provide Regional failover.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: Global Accelerator accepts traffic on fixed Anycast IP addresses and can route TCP traffic to healthy endpoints.
learning.concept: Global Accelerator accepts traffic on fixed Anycast IP addresses and forwards TCP traffic to healthy endpoints, such as NLBs in healthy Regions. It does not guarantee that existing connections will be transferred without interruption during a failure.

check.prompt: Does lowering the Route 53 TTL provide an equivalent fixed ingress point?
check.answer: No. It depends on clients resolving DNS again and does not provide a shared, fixed Anycast ingress point.

title: SMB compatibility
prompt: A business application running on Windows EC2 instances accesses shared files. SMB, existing Active Directory groups, and Windows ACLs are required, and the service must fail over during an AZ outage.

choices.text: Deploy Amazon FSx for Windows File Server in a Multi-AZ configuration and join it to Active Directory
choices.explanation: It can maintain the service across AZs while using SMB and Windows ACLs.

choices.text: Use Amazon EFS Regional as a direct SMB share for Windows clients
choices.explanation: EFS is an NFS service and does not meet the existing SMB and Windows ACL requirements.

choices.text: Configure S3 directly as a UNC path
choices.explanation: A business application cannot use S3's object API as SMB.

choices.text: Expose SMB from a single Windows EC2 instance and replicate only EBS snapshots
choices.explanation: This does not provide managed Multi-AZ failover during an outage.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: It can maintain the service across AZs while using SMB and Windows ACLs.
learning.concept: FSx for Windows File Server supports Windows ACLs. In a Multi-AZ configuration, it fails over to a standby file server in another AZ.

check.prompt: Does a Single-AZ backup provide the same result?
