check.answer: It can be used to restore data, but it is not automatic failover; restoration to a new environment is required.

title: Temporary workspace for HPC
prompt: Hundreds of Linux compute nodes need to read and write shared working files in parallel while using reference data in S3. High parallel throughput is required, and the output must be returned to S3 after processing. The file transfer management must also be handled by a managed feature.

choices.text: Distribute output across each node's instance store and treat it as shared files
choices.explanation: Individual local disks do not provide a shared namespace.

choices.text: Associate FSx for Lustre with an S3 data repository
choices.explanation: This provides an HPC parallel file system and integration with a data repository.

choices.text: Mount EFS Regional and use the AWS CLI on each node to synchronize with S3 in both directions
choices.explanation: This provides shared POSIX storage, but it does not combine Lustre for high-parallel-I/O workloads with native integration to an S3 data repository.

choices.text: Connect one EC2 instance's EBS volume as a local device on all nodes
choices.explanation: This does not provide an HPC shared file system across many nodes.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: This provides an HPC parallel file system and integration with a data repository.
learning.concept: FSx for Lustre is designed for parallel I/O. Associating it with an S3 data repository lets you manage imports and exports between S3 objects and the file system.

check.prompt: Would having each node copy data from S3 independently provide the same architecture?
check.answer: No. There would be no shared namespace, and you would have to manage synchronization on each node.

title: DynamoDB query patterns
prompt: The DynamoDB partition key is the order ID. Delivery staff frequently search by warehouse ID and a range of shipping deadlines. The existing primary key must remain unchanged, and eventual consistency is acceptable. Which approach avoids a full table scan?

choices.text: Add a FilterExpression for warehouse ID and deadline to a Scan
choices.explanation: The filter is applied after items are read, so the scan itself is still required.

choices.text: Create an LSI that keeps order ID as the partition key and uses only warehouse ID as the sort key
choices.explanation: An LSI query still requires specifying the order ID.

choices.text: Move the Scan to DAX and create no index
choices.explanation: Caching does not provide a key structure suited to the search criteria.

choices.text: Create a GSI with warehouse ID as the partition key and shipping deadline as the sort key, then use Query
choices.explanation: This directly searches the required range by warehouse and deadline.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: This directly searches the required range by warehouse and deadline.
learning.concept: A GSI can use a partition key different from that of the base table. Use Query with the warehouse ID and deadline. A filter is applied after items are read.

check.prompt: What happens if you add a deadline filter to a GSI that has only warehouse ID as its key?
check.answer: A Scan can be avoided, but items for that warehouse outside the deadline range are still read before being excluded.

title: CloudFront cache efficiency
prompt: A version query parameter changes only when the image content changes. Analytics utm parameters have many values but do not affect the image content. You want to distinguish old and new versions while improving the cache hit ratio.

choices.text: Apply a cache policy that includes only version in the cache key
choices.explanation: Separating only by the parameter that changes the content lets requests with different utm values use the same cache entry.

choices.text: Include all query parameters in the cache key
choices.explanation: Differences in utm values split the same image into separate entries.

choices.text: Include no query parameters and set a long TTL
choices.explanation: The old and new versions at the same path would have the same cache key.

choices.text: Disable caching for all requests
choices.explanation: Although each version can be retrieved, this does not meet the requirement to improve the hit ratio.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: Separating only by the parameter that changes the content lets requests with different utm values use the same cache entry.
learning.concept: The values included in the cache key and those forwarded to the origin can be configured separately. Query parameters included in the cache key are also forwarded to the origin.

check.prompt: What happens if version is forwarded to the origin but is not included in the cache key?
check.answer: The response may be correct on a cache miss, but a response for a different version could be returned from the existing cache.

title: Unpredictable S3 access
prompt: The video assets to be stored are at least 4 MiB. Access frequency varies greatly by project, and moving objects to an infrequent-access tier after a fixed number of days makes retrieval costs unpredictable. All assets must be retrievable in milliseconds at any time.

choices.text: Move objects to Standard-IA exactly 30 days after creation and retrieve them as usual
choices.explanation: Variable access can result in retrieval charges.

choices.text: Move objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive immediately after creation and restore them when needed
choices.explanation: This does not meet the immediate-read requirement.

choices.text: Use S3 Intelligent-Tiering without enabling the optional asynchronous archive tiers
choices.explanation: It moves objects between tiers based on access patterns and maintains millisecond access without retrieval charges.

choices.text: Move all data used for specific projects to One Zone-IA
choices.explanation: A fixed infrequent-access tier does not adapt to changing patterns and also has retrieval charges.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: It moves objects between tiers based on access patterns and maintains millisecond access without retrieval charges.
learning.concept: S3 Intelligent-Tiering moves objects between tiers based on access patterns. Monitoring and automation incur charges. Objects in the optional asynchronous archive tiers must be restored before retrieval.

check.prompt: Can Deep Archive Access be enabled while preserving immediate retrieval?
check.answer: No. Objects moved to that tier must be restored first, so do not enable it when this requirement applies.

title: EC2 and Fargate costs
prompt: You want to continue covering baseline EC2 usage with a commitment-based discount. Some workloads are planned to migrate to Fargate within six months, and the EC2 instance family is also planned to change. Limit the commitment to the predictable minimum spend.

choices.text: Purchase EC2 Instance Savings Plans for the current family
choices.explanation: They do not cover a change beyond that family’s scope or Fargate.

choices.text: Purchase Compute Savings Plans only up to the amount of the minimum spend
choices.explanation: They accommodate changes in eligible EC2 usage and also apply to Fargate.

choices.text: Purchase zonal Reserved Instances for the current EC2 usage at peak capacity
choices.explanation: They cannot follow the migration to Fargate, and the commitment exceeds the minimum usage.

choices.text: Create an On-Demand Capacity Reservation for the minimum capacity
choices.explanation: It can reserve capacity, but does not itself provide a long-term discount.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: They accommodate changes in eligible EC2 usage and also apply to Fargate.
learning.concept: Compute Savings Plans commit to an hourly spend and can apply to eligible EC2, Fargate, and Lambda usage. EC2 Instance Savings Plans have a narrower scope.

check.prompt: Why commit to the stable minimum usage rather than the peak?
check.answer: You pay for any unused commitment. If variable usage is committed too, some of it may go unused when demand falls.

title: Run batch jobs safely with Spot
prompt: The overnight job can save checkpoints to S3, and even if it is interrupted, it can still meet its acceptable deadline. You want to use EC2 spare capacity at a discount while avoiding a situation where a shortage of one instance type stops the entire job.

choices.text: Configure multiple instance families and multiple Availability Zones as Spot capacity options
choices.explanation: This increases the number of available Spot pools and reduces reliance on any one pool.

choices.text: Restrict Spot to a single instance type in a single Availability Zone
choices.explanation: This makes the job depend on one capacity pool.

choices.text: Write checkpoints only to ephemeral instance storage
choices.explanation: After an instance interruption, another instance cannot access them.

choices.text: Use a Spot allocation strategy that considers both price and capacity, and resume from persistent checkpoints
choices.explanation: This reduces interruption risk and lets processing resume on a different instance.

choices.text: Purchase EC2 Instance Savings Plans and apply them to Spot charges
choices.explanation: Savings Plans do not apply to Spot usage charges.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: This increases the number of available Spot pools and reduces reliance on any one pool. It also reduces interruption risk and lets processing resume on a different instance.
learning.concept: A Spot pool is a combination of instance type and Availability Zone. Use alternative capacity options and an allocation strategy that considers both price and capacity. Checkpoints prepare the workload to resume after an interruption.

check.prompt: Can persistent checkpoints prevent Spot interruptions themselves?
check.answer: No. They help limit lost work and resume the job on different capacity after an interruption.

title: Unnecessary NAT processing
prompt: A private EC2 instance transfers several terabytes to S3 in the same Region every day. It also uses the same NAT gateway to reach external APIs, so the NAT gateway cannot be removed. You want to eliminate NAT processing charges attributable to S3 transfers. Access is from the same VPC, and you also want to avoid new endpoint processing charges.

choices.text: Route all traffic through an S3 interface endpoint
choices.explanation: This avoids NAT, but interface endpoints have hourly and data processing charges. For access from the same VPC, a free gateway endpoint costs less.

choices.text: Add more Elastic IP addresses to the NAT gateway
choices.explanation: This might ease connection limits, but S3 traffic would still traverse the NAT gateway and incur processing charges.

choices.text: Add an S3 gateway endpoint to the EC2 instance's route table
choices.explanation: This routes only traffic for the S3 prefix away from NAT, while external API calls can continue to use NAT.

choices.text: Use a CloudFront distribution as the upload destination
choices.explanation: This does not solve the problem of traffic from the private EC2 instance to the public edge traversing NAT.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: This routes only traffic for the S3 prefix away from NAT, while external API calls can continue to use NAT.
learning.concept: For an S3 gateway endpoint in the same Region, add a route for the S3 destination prefix. Gateway endpoints have no endpoint hourly or data processing charges.

check.prompt: Can you remove NAT after changing the route to S3?
check.answer: No. Under these conditions, external API calls still use NAT.

title: Separate EBS capacity from performance
prompt: You use a 2 TiB gp2 volume, but your data occupies 800 GiB. You chose the larger capacity to get 6,000 IOPS. You want to keep the required performance while lowering the cost of unneeded capacity.

choices.text: Use ModifyVolume to shrink the existing gp2 volume to 1 TiB
choices.explanation: EBS does not let you shrink an existing volume this way, and gp2 baseline IOPS also depends on volume size.

choices.text: Create a smaller gp3 volume with the required IOPS and throughput, migrate the data, and switch over
choices.explanation: With gp3, capacity and performance can be configured independently.

choices.text: Restore the existing snapshot directly to a 1 TiB gp3 volume
choices.explanation: You cannot directly restore a snapshot to a volume smaller than the original volume.

choices.text: Change the volume to st1 and use burst performance for random I/O
choices.explanation: st1 is not suitable for sustained, high-IOPS random I/O requirements.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: With gp3, capacity and performance can be configured independently.
learning.concept: With gp3, you can specify performance independently of capacity. You cannot shrink an existing EBS volume, and a snapshot cannot be restored directly to a volume smaller than the original.

check.prompt: Can you halve capacity charges just by changing gp2 to gp3 in place?
check.answer: No. The capacity stays the same. You need to migrate the data to a new, smaller volume.

title: Long-term log storage costs
prompt: Audit logs are accessed frequently for the first 30 days and then about once a year. From day 31 onward, retrieval within 48 hours is acceptable, and the logs must be retained for 7 years. The objects are at least several MiB in size.

choices.text: Use S3 Standard for the entire retention period
choices.explanation: This costs more than needed for infrequently accessed, long-term storage.

choices.text: Transition to S3 Standard-IA after 30 days and keep the logs there
choices.explanation: Millisecond access is not required, and a lower-cost archive class is available for the long retention period.

choices.text: Transition to S3 Glacier Deep Archive immediately after creation
choices.explanation: This is not suitable for frequent reads during the first 30 days.

choices.text: Transition from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 30 days
choices.explanation: This preserves immediate access at first and then provides a low storage rate with a 48-hour retrieval allowance.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: This preserves immediate access at first and then provides a low storage rate with a 48-hour retrieval allowance.
learning.concept: S3 Glacier Deep Archive requires a restore before a normal GET request. Typical retrieval times vary by retrieval option; Bulk retrieval is typically within 48 hours.

check.prompt: What if logs must be available immediately after day 30?
check.answer: Deep Archive would not be suitable. Compare the storage and retrieval charges of classes that provide immediate access.

title: Irregular DynamoDB Traffic
prompt: A new DynamoDB service has occasional short bursts of traffic but very little access most of the time. Peak demand cannot be predicted in advance, and capacity cannot be adjusted manually. Assume the growth rate remains within the on-demand scaling range.

choices.text: Use on-demand capacity mode
choices.explanation: It charges per request and can adapt to variable demand without preallocating capacity.

choices.text: Always provision capacity for the peak
choices.explanation: You pay for provisioned capacity even during quiet periods.

choices.text: Set low provisioned capacity with a long scaling cooldown
choices.explanation: This makes throttling more likely immediately after a sudden burst begins.

choices.text: Replace the table with DAX
choices.explanation: DAX does not replace the DynamoDB persistent store and incurs separate cluster charges.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: It charges per request and can adapt to variable demand without preallocating capacity.
learning.concept: DynamoDB on-demand billing scales with request volume. It can still throttle traffic outside its scaling range, such as a sudden increase far beyond the previous peak.

check.prompt: Does switching to on-demand mean that any increase, no matter how large, can be handled without limits?
check.answer: No. Check the previous peak, quotas, key distribution, and other factors.

sourceLabel: AWS Official Exam Guide (exam content outline)

title: Log Queries and Retention
prompt: Logs used for incident analysis are accumulating indefinitely in CloudWatch Logs. Immediate searches are needed only for the most recent 14 days. Regulations require retention for one year, but older logs are queried only a few times per year, and the ingestion path must not change.

choices.text: Set only the CloudWatch Logs retention period to 14 days
choices.explanation: Without a separate archive, this would also lose historical data required by regulations.

choices.text: Continuously deliver the required logs to S3 and transition older logs to a lower-cost storage tier
choices.explanation: This separates storage for the period that does not require immediate searches.

choices.text: Use CloudWatch Logs Insights extensively to reduce storage costs
choices.explanation: Running queries does not change the retention period or the amount of data stored.

choices.text: Use Glacier retrieval alone to replace immediate 14-day search in CloudWatch Logs
choices.explanation: Because retrieval is required, this does not meet the everyday immediate-search requirement.

choices.text: Verify that existing logs have been backfilled to S3, then set the CloudWatch Logs retention period to 14 days
choices.explanation: This reduces storage costs for immediate-search data without losing the history that must be retained for one year.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: This separates storage for the period that does not require immediate searches. It reduces storage costs for immediate-search data without losing the history that must be retained for one year.
learning.concept: Subscriptions can continuously deliver new logs, while S3 export can be used to migrate existing logs. Verify that the transition has no gaps or duplicates before changing the retention setting.

check.prompt: If you create a subscription now, will it also move logs from six months ago?
check.answer: No. Plan a separate retrospective transfer.

sourceLabel: AWS Official Exam Guide (exam content outline)

title: Incomplete S3 Uploads
prompt: Clients abandon multipart uploads partway through when using unreliable connections, so S3 storage grows disproportionately to the number of completed objects. Normal uploads complete within 24 hours.

choices.text: Expire current objects after two days
choices.explanation: This setting applies to completed objects; use a dedicated rule to delete incomplete parts.

choices.text: Delete S3 delete markers
choices.explanation: Incomplete parts are unrelated to delete markers.

choices.text: Use a lifecycle rule to abort incomplete multipart uploads more than two days after initiation
choices.explanation: This removes parts from old incomplete uploads while leaving normal uploads time to finish.

choices.text: Configure S3 Intelligent-Tiering to move incomplete parts
choices.explanation: Incomplete parts cannot be deleted by transitioning objects between storage tiers.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: This removes parts from old incomplete uploads while leaving normal uploads time to finish.
learning.concept: The lifecycle action AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload stops incomplete uploads after the specified number of days from initiation. It is separate from expiration of completed objects.

check.prompt: If normal uploads take three days, is it safe to abort them after two days?
check.answer: Normal uploads could also be aborted. Set the threshold longer than the time needed for normal processing.

sourceLabel: AWS Official Exam Guide (exam content outline)

title: Idle Costs in an Analytics Environment
prompt: Small-scale SQL analytics run a few times per week. The source data is Parquet in S3, the queries use standard SQL, and some job startup delay is acceptable. The solution must eliminate always-on server costs and set a scan-volume limit for each department.

choices.text: Run Presto continuously on EC2 and share it across departments
choices.explanation: EC2 costs accrue during idle time, even for intermittent workloads.

choices.text: Use Athena on-demand queries, with a workgroup and scan-volume limit for each department
choices.explanation: This avoids keeping servers provisioned at all times and controls the amount scanned per query.

choices.text: Use a provisioned Redshift cluster continuously
choices.explanation: You pay for cluster capacity even when it is idle.

choices.text: Embed standard SQL in AWS Glue Spark jobs and share a common execution pool across departments
choices.explanation: This can avoid idle charges, but meeting the requirement for an Athena-equivalent scan-volume limit would require additional implementation.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: This avoids keeping servers provisioned at all times and controls the amount scanned per query.
learning.concept: Athena reads S3 data directly with SQL. For on-demand queries, scanned data is a key cost driver, and a per-query workgroup limit can stop queries that exceed it.

check.prompt: Can a workgroup's per-query limit be treated as a monthly spending cap for a department?
check.answer: No. A per-query limit is separate from monitoring cumulative monthly costs or usage.

title: Image generation management
prompt: A large number of images are pushed to ECR, one per commit. Release images must be retained for 90 days to support production rollbacks, while only the 10 most recent CI tags generated each time should be kept. Each image has a single tag identifying its purpose.

choices.text: Automatically delete old images during ECR scans
choices.explanation: Image scanning detects vulnerabilities; it does not manage retained image generations.

choices.text: Delete images when the repository contains more than 10 images
choices.explanation: This could unintentionally violate the 90-day retention requirement for production releases.

choices.text: Replicate all CI and release images to separate accounts
choices.explanation: This does not meet the retention policies and consumes additional storage.

choices.text: Create ECR lifecycle policies for each purpose-specific tag prefix
choices.explanation: Images can be deleted based on count for CI and age for releases.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: Images can be deleted based on count for CI and age for releases.
learning.concept: ECR lifecycle policies combine tag criteria with a count or age threshold. Rules target images, so review the evaluation results when an image can have multiple tags.

check.prompt: What if CI and release tags are attached to the same image?
check.answer: The current assumption no longer holds. Recheck whether the release image is included, along with rule priority and the preview results.

title: Long-running containers on a schedule
prompt: A container workload runs for two hours only a few times a month. You want to avoid managing hosts and incur compute charges only while the workload runs. It must start at a fixed time, and Spot capacity reclamation during processing is not acceptable.

choices.text: Call ECS RunTask from EventBridge Scheduler and run it on standard Fargate capacity
choices.explanation: The task runs only when launched, no host management is required, and Spot reclamation is not assumed.

choices.text: Run the container for two hours as a single Lambda invocation
choices.explanation: A single Lambda invocation can run for at most 15 minutes.

choices.text: Place the container on an always-on EC2 instance and start it with cron
choices.explanation: EC2 charges continue while idle, and host management is still required.

choices.text: Schedule a task on Fargate Spot
choices.explanation: Capacity reclamation can terminate the task before it finishes.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: The task runs only when launched, no host management is required, and Spot reclamation is not assumed.
learning.concept: EventBridge Scheduler invokes ECS RunTask at the specified time. With standard Fargate capacity, you do not need to manage underlying EC2 instances or keep a minimum number of service tasks running.

check.prompt: Are successful task launch and successful task completion the same thing?
check.answer: No. A job can fail even after RunTask is accepted, so observe the task's final status.

title: Reducing NAT charges for service access
prompt: Workers in several private subnets communicate only with DynamoDB within AWS. The roadmap includes no external connectivity, and the VPC processes several TB. The workers and table are in the same AWS Region.

choices.text: Keep a public NAT gateway and move it to the same AZ as the workers
choices.explanation: This can reduce cross-AZ charges, but NAT hourly and data processing charges remain.

choices.text: Associate a DynamoDB gateway endpoint and remove the NAT gateways that have no other use
choices.explanation: This preserves connectivity while eliminating unnecessary NAT charges.

choices.text: Create DynamoDB Accelerator and route all NAT-based access through DAX
choices.explanation: DAX adds node charges and is not intended to replace the path for all DynamoDB operations.

choices.text: Move the network to NAT instances
choices.explanation: Instance costs and operational work remain, making this more burdensome than a service-specific endpoint that meets the requirements.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: This preserves connectivity while eliminating unnecessary NAT charges.
learning.concept: A DynamoDB gateway endpoint is associated with route tables in a VPC. A gateway endpoint in a shared VPC cannot be used transitively through a TGW.

check.prompt: What if you only move the NAT gateways to each worker VPC?
check.answer: TGW charges may be avoided, but NAT data processing charges for DynamoDB traffic remain.
